questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.**

It is imperative in understanding / the rising importance of artificial intelligence / in the public sector to increase the efficacy / and impact of the work done for public welfare.

options.text: the rising importance of artificial intelligence
and impact of the work done for public welfare.
in the public sector to increase the efficacy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**It is imperative in understanding**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error is in the use of the phrase "**in understanding**." It should be "**to understand**" instead.
 
• "**To understand**" is more direct and clear, specifying the action that is imperative. 
 
• "**Imperative to**" is a more common and idiomatic construction when expressing the necessity or importance of an action.
 
• The use of "**to understand**" maintains grammatical consistency with the structure of the sentence.
 
• The construction "to understand" is an example of the "**to + infinitive**" form of the verb.
 
• In English, the infinitive form of a verb is the base form preceded by the particle "**to**."
 
• By using "**to understand**," the sentence flows more smoothly and conveys the idea that understanding the rising importance of artificial intelligence is imperative for achieving the desired outcomes in the public sector.

Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. These changes were sure to happen as technological intervention cannot be arrested anywhere.

B. Recent times have marked a major change in the teaching-learning process in the educational sector.

C. A willing acceptance and practicing it to achieve excellence into it is the single option to all educators.

D. Beyond this, the constant flux in the diversified areas of academics has forced this change.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **B, A, D, C**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

 
• **Sentence B** introduces the topic of the paragraph, which is the changes in the teaching-learning process in the educational sector.
 
• **Sentence A** explains that these changes were bound to happen due to technological advancements.
 
• **Sentence D** provides further explanation by stating that the constant evolution in academics has also contributed to these changes.
 
• **Sentence C** concludes the paragraph by suggesting that educators must willingly accept and embrace these changes to excel in their profession.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

She will accept his love proposal __if he will express__ impressively.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**If he expresses**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In English, conditional sentences often use the present simple tense in the "**if**" clause.
 
• This is because the action in the "**if**" clause (expressing love impressively, in this case) is generally a habitual or factual condition.
 
• Therefore, the usage of "**if he expresses**" is more appropriate than "**if he will express**."
 
• "**Expresses**" is in the present simple tense and is commonly used in conditional sentences to indicate a general truth or habitual action.
 
• This emphasizes that the person (he) is actively involved in expressing his feelings.

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.**

Everyone should be aware of the possibly greater __potential__ for natural disasters where they live and what resources they have in case these happen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Certainty**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence talks about being aware of the possibility of natural disasters.
 
• **Potential: **The capability or possibility for something to happen or develop; having the capacity or ability. (किसी चीज़ के घटित होने या विकसित होने की क्षमता या संभावना; क्षमता या योग्यता होना)
 
 
• **Example**: *His potential as a leader became evident when he successfully led the team to victory.*
 
 
 
• Marked option **Certainty: **The state of being certain, sure, or confident about something; the quality of being definite or unquestionable. (किसी चीज़ के बारे में निश्चित, सुनिश्चित या आश्वस्त होने की अवस्था; निश्चित या निर्विवाद होने का गुण)
 
 
• **Example**: *The scientific experiment yielded conclusive results, providing a high level of certainty about the hypothesis.*
 
 
 
• Hence, the antonym of 'potential' is 'certainty'.

Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:

• The correct preposition to use in this context is "**of**." 
 
• The phrase "**on behalf of**" is used to indicate representing or in the interest of someone or something.
 
• It is a fixed expression and the preposition "**of**" is the correct choice to follow it.
 
• **Corrected Sentence**: "*The soldier met a fearless death fighting on behalf of his country.*"
 
• The corrected sentence uses "**on behalf of his country**," which is the appropriate and idiomatic way to express that the soldier was fighting for the interests or in the name of his country.

Thus, **option 4** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in superlative degree of comparison.**

options.text: This type is the quiet and efficient style of humidifier.
